Flicked like a whip, it throws large thorns coated with azure sap that promotes blood loss, or can be used like a short whip in close combat. Thrown use: Acc +3, 8L, Rate 2, Range 20; like a target arrow it is armor-piercing, and anyone wounded loses one health level every 10 turns due to bleeding, with all attempts to stop it at +1 difficulty. Hand-to-hand: Speed +4, Acc +2, +6L, Def +3, Min D•••. Each ranged attack costs 1 additional mote.

name: Boot Grafts
description: Amorphous masses of fibrous tissue covered in tiny spines that expand over the feet to the ankles and harden into bark-like 'boots' with large spines where the toes would be. They provide solid support, warmth in cold conditions and aeration in hot conditions, and grant a +2 bonus to all Athletics checks involving climbing or mounting an incline. Photosynthetic, they survive on at least four hours of bright sunlight a day; dormant grafts require 1 mote and four hours of direct sunlight to reactivate.

name: Breather Plant
description: A small leafy vine that wraps around the neck of a living being no larger than a war horse, growing tendrils into the neck that let the wearer breathe both fresh and salt water (but not poisoned or extremely stagnant bodies of water). After roughly three hours of use it slowly yellows and goes dormant, and must be returned to its pot for at least 12 hours before it can be used again.

name: Green Eyes
description: Translucent cylindrical plants that spread very thinly over the wearer's eyes. For six hours after application the wearer is effectively blinded while the buds adapt; afterwards they grant clarity of vision to see details 100 yards distant without difficulty, plus one automatic success on Awareness rolls (these benefits do not add to those granted by Awareness Charms). They require 1 mote per day, otherwise they revert to an inert state and fall from the eyes.

name: Green Iron Dust
description: Pollen from the hraas'kaztha plant ground to a fine powder and ingested. It adds a dot to Strength and Stamina for one scene, as well as to the Brawl, Endurance, Dodge, Melee and Resistance Abilities, at the cost of 1 dot in Wits (which does not affect initiative). Afterwards the character suffers the loss of 1 dot in Strength, Dexterity and Wits for one hour. Typically found in containers of 100 doses, fewer naturally having a lower Artifact value at the Storyteller's discretion.

name: Knife Spores
description: Tiny ambulatory plants native to the subterranean regions around Rathess, with flat bodies and sharp filaments covering their surface. A colony that infests a living creature (at the cost of one lethal health level per day) lets the character inflict lethal rather than bashing damage with his blows. After 10 successful blows while wearing them, the spores die in large enough numbers to be ineffectual.

name: Healing Orchid
description: A finger-thick vine encircling the wearer's arm, bearing several dozen thumb-sized leaves and half a dozen emerald-green flowers, that lets the wearer heal far faster than normal. Exalts wearing it heal one level of bashing damage per hour or one level of lethal damage every three hours, and roll two additional dice to resist poison, disease or infection. Dragon Kings and Exalts must commit 4 motes of Essence to keep it healthy; mortal humans must instead eat three times as much food whenever it is active, and unExalted wearers need a Stamina of at least 4 to support it.

name: Vine Klave
description: A five-foot weapon with a two-foot gnarly woody haft and a three-foot blade of vine specially bred to be as tough as fine steel; when inactive the fibrous blade becomes flexible and coils along the haft. Placing its thorns against flesh extends and coils them around the arm, causing a short piercing pain and unsoakably draining two health levels that cannot be recovered until the weapon is detached. Once attached the wearer cannot be disarmed or drop it, but the limited grip adds +1 difficulty on all rolls involving the physical dexterity of that hand and prevents picking anything else up. Stats: Speed +3, Acc +2, +5L, Def +0, Min S•.

name: Mimic Skin
description: A viscous globule of transparent fleshy material held in a small cylindrical orichalcum container. Infused with 3 motes of Essence it expands and crawls over a normal-sized person from head to foot, leaving all senses and breathing unobstructed while it mimics its surroundings: anyone trying to see the wearer suffers a four-dice penalty to Perception + Awareness rolls if the wearer stays perfectly still, reduced to two dice if he is moving. It stays active for three days, then must regenerate its matrix in its container for three more before it can be activated again.
rating_notes: ••• per the page; the worklist lists ••

name: Sun Crystal
description: Small, regularly shaped crystals that occur naturally in Southern lands, often underground or on the surface after volcanic eruptions. With the expenditure of 1 mote a crystal glows brightly and clearly for 1,001 days, illuminating an area 90 feet in diameter; an additional mote increases the radius to 150 feet, and expending any more shatters the crystal in an impressive (though harmless) pyrotechnic display.

name: Lizard Tail Regrowth Sphere
description: A glittering green globe laced with red stripes and full of warm, translucent green slime. Those placed within it heal at 20 times the normal rate, whether lethal or bashing, and regrow lost limbs and appendages as if under the effects of Bodily Regeneration Prana: small appendages take (10 - Stamina) days, minimum 1, and limbs take (21 - Stamina) days, minimum 3. Proper use requires at least 1 dot of Medicine (3 dots to regenerate a limb); the technician commits 10 motes, and each activation consumes a one-use tube of herbal and alchemical reagents costing Resources •••.

name: Warbird
description: A vehicle of living magical metals shaped like a giant hawk, eagle, owl, raiton or bat, controlled with leg movements, weight shifting, built-in reins and verbal commands (Dexterity + Ride). It carries up to two passengers on saddles, flies at 120 miles per hour (100 yards per turn in combat), has 10 health levels and 10L/15B soak, and protects riders with the equivalent of 75 percent hard cover against attacks from below and a target shield against all other attacks, with all attacks on it at an additional +2 difficulty. A Hearthstone of at least level 2 is needed to awaken it; inactive it appears to be an immobile metal statue.

name: Enchiridion of All Knowledge
description: A short work created through supernatural scrivenery by Auspicious Plume that contains far more information than its pages should allow, covering a wide variety of First Age topics in an extremely curt, almanac-like fashion. It adds +3 to Lore for discovering superficial facts about the First Age, but provides no bonus for the sort of material that could not be found in an almanac or dictionary. Composed only once (though frequently copied), it dates from the mid First Age.

name: Glory to the Ghoul King
description: A Dragon King crystal 'book' — a thin square of black stony material with a glass plate on one side. Infused with 3 motes of Essence, the plate lights up displaying sigils in the High Holy Speech, readable as scrolling text. A religious text dedicated to the worship of Han-Tha, the Eater of the Dead, its graphic descriptions of his rites (including necrophagy) provide many insights into his dark cult; reading it requires knowing the High Holy Speech and a difficulty 3 Perception + Lore roll to understand the esoteric jargon.

name: Arc Protector
description: Goggles faced with black crystal created by Luminor savants. Wearers can see in normal illumination and suffer no penalties or negative repercussions from staring at naked electrical arcs, open plasma furnaces and the like, though the goggles provide no protection against magic that happens to have a visual component and hamper vision in low-light conditions (a dice penalty of one to three).

name: Autolabe
description: A navigational device: the gimbaled pointer in an autolabe points back to a fixed beacon, just as a jade needle compass points to the Elemental Pole of Earth in Creation. The beacon can be reset by leaving the autolabe in physical contact with a new beacon for 25 hours; exploration models come as a set with a base unit, and a rare variant has two autolabes always point back to one another. Most autolabes are spheres approximately three inches in diameter.
rating_notes: • or ••

name: Essence Capacitor
description: Elaborate polyhedral crystal jewels an inch wide fitted in a wire cage of orichalcum and condensed Primordial Essence, filling the technological niche Hearthstones serve in Creation (Autochthonia has no Demesnes or Manses). A working capacitor may be plugged into the sockets of large or advanced artifacts to supply constant power, exactly as a Hearthstone. Virtually indestructible, if broken they release a devastating pulse of the capacitor's rating x 10L damage (minus 1L per full yard away). They function for 25 hours before shutting down, recharge one hour for every two spent respiring Essence in Autochthonia, and must be calibrated to respire in other realms.

name: Flaw Scanner
description: A disc-shaped amulet of carved amethyst an inch wide locked in a ring of orichalcum, worn on one hand so the jewel is centered against the palm. Activated for a scene by expending 1 Willpower or 2 motes, it projects a narrow cone of soft violet light in which any cracks, flaws or points of unintended stress appear highlighted in a bright purple-white aura, scanning up to a square yard each turn. Craft rolls made to repair detected flaws add a one-die bonus so long as the technician studies the damage for a full minute under the light.

name: Light Amplification Visor
description: Goggles with a pair of narrow lenses or a single curved lens extending across both eyes. Wearers constantly receive the benefits and drawbacks provided by the light-intensification filters submodule of the Optical Enhancement Charm; some mortals have small versions surgically implanted in their eyes (three-hour surgery, Intelligence + Medicine at difficulty 5, permanent blindness on failure). Artifact •• versions provide thermal vision when powered — 1 Willpower charges the lenses for two hours, while a mote charges them for one hour. Alchemicals cannot have these artifacts implanted, although other varieties of Exalted may.
rating_notes: • or ••

name: Light Sphere
description: Three-inch-wide globes of brass and tempered glass containing a treated orichalcum catalyst and a socket for inserting coin-sized discs of low-quality jade. The catalyst makes the jade sublime away in a slow incandescent display with the radiance of a torch, yet without heat or smoke. Each jade fuel disc (Resources • in Autochthonia or Yu-Shan, •• elsewhere) produces light for a full week; higher-quality discs last a month and perfectly calibrated ones a year. Rarer models (also Artifact •) have an articulated iris shutter and colored glass filters used for signaling, tripling the distance of illumination as a narrow cone.

name: Omnimodal Wardrobe Unit
description: An entire wardrobe compressed into a single garment, appearing by default as a basic citizen uniform of artificial silk that is unusually light, glossy oil black and faintly iridescent, with a fine lattice of moonsilver wires. Attuned for 1 committed mote, it changes form with a thought: each change is a reflexive action costing 1 mote, as hundreds of thumbnail-sized spider automata weave and transmute the fibers into the new template in a single turn, also cleaning and repairing any damage. It can become any clothing type from a single glove to a full outfit; in all forms it is unusually durable (+1L soak, not armor or natural soak, cumulative with armor), but it can only become clothes, never actual armor.

name: Portable Nutriment Recycling Engine
description: A machine approximately the size of a person and weighing a mere 30 pounds, with a clockwork power cell and a foot-wide intake chute on top; pressing a button collapses it into a rectangular steel box that fits in a backpack. Wound with a crank (five minutes of winding produces an hour of operation), spinning blades chew any organic material fed into the intake chute, and every two pounds of organic substance takes one minute to process into a thumbnail-sized white pellet that provides the same nourishment as a full meal. All toxins and diseases present in the matter are removed before the pellets emerge; ten pellets are a Resources •• item in Autochthonia.

name: Respirator Module
description: Sophisticated filter masks with a central nodule of blue jade surrounded by wires of mystical alloys, usable as filter masks without any cleaning or upkeep. Flipping a switch with the tongue seals the device and synthesizes air out of Essence, completely protecting the user against harmful airborne effects and allowing travel underwater or through a vacuum without asphyxiating. Each chip of crystallized thaumaturgical reagent (Resources •• for a batch of 10) provides an hour of air; beings able to channel Essence may spend a mote reflexively to power it for an hour.

name: Courier Drone
description: Three-inch-long automata reminiscent of large metallic dragonflies, one of the most common means of delivering messages between Autochthonian cities. They carry up to a quarter-pound of weight, navigate by Essence to track the emissions of metropoli, and fly at a top speed of 300 miles per hour. A less common exploration and military version (also Artifact ••) flies back and forth between two rings, infallibly tracking their target beacons in real time so long as they are on the same plane of reality.

name: Soulgem
description: Every citizen of the Eight Nations receives one within a week of birth: needle-sharp soulsteel posts drive into the center of the forehead, and the gem is fused to skull and nerve with a touch of a living nerve of the Great Maker. When its bearer dies, the jewel absorbs her still-fused higher and lower soul and stores it until the spirit can be recycled; the Essence of a Celestial Exalt cannot be captured. Soulgems are as durable as Hearthstones, and deliberately breaking one is a capital crime throughout Autochthonia. Players do not spend Background points for one — everyone is assumed to have it.

name: Industrial Exoskeleton
description: A humanoid frame of steel and magical alloys close to 12 feet tall, covered in plates of armor over clockwork machinery, with long four-part vice pincer arms and articulated plate claws. A human or Essence 2-3 Alchemical climbs in; after a wire filament threads up into her brain, committing 8 motes (or 2 Willpower for beings unable to channel Essence) makes the exoskeleton an extension of her body. It adds 12 to Strength for lifting, breaking and strength-based damage, and counts as armor with soak 12L/12B (hardness 6L/6B), mobility penalty -8 and fatigue 2 (lighter unarmored models: soak 6L/6B, mobility -3, fatigue 1); heavily armored models halve the user's ground speed and cannot jump or climb. Requires a two-dot Essence capacitor installed to function at all.

name: Fibre-Weave Bodysuit
description: A light armor of high-quality fiber-weave threaded with a lattice of wires or embedded nodes of Magical Materials, extremely supple and thin and roughly equivalent to an enchanted chain shirt. It requires a commitment of 3 motes and is intended for discreet or covert situations, since it can be worn under normal clothes. Lethal piercing attacks based on actual kinetic penetration do not halve the armor's soak unless the raw damage is at least twice the base lethal soak. Artifact •• versions also incorporate all the properties of an omnimodal wardrobe unit except its soak bonus, with the same 3-mote attunement.
rating_notes: • or ••

name: Gyroscopic Chakram
description: Six-inch metal disks with five holes spread for gripping, the most widely used and feared thrown weapons of the Alchemical Exalted, normally carried strapped to the small of the back or the side of the thigh. Hurled by an attuned owner (5-mote commitment), clockwork deploys a ring of three-inch blades that spin at high velocity and the disk banks to follow its quarry: if it misses due to a dodge or parry it swoops back for another attempt on the following turn, acting at initiative 20 with a pool of 10 dice until it hits or botches, then arcs back to its owner's hand at the end of the turn. Additional powers depend on the Magical Material used to make it, and the disks can also be used in close combat as saws.

name: Beam-Klave
description: The signature melee weapons of the Alchemical Exalted: unassuming cylinders of reinforced alloys and Magical Materials tipped with a small crystal spike, most between 9 and 12 inches long. Once attuned for a commitment of 3 motes, an additional 5 motes per scene extends a blade of glowing Essence from the jewel to an average length of three feet, combining heat and pure force; the blade can set flammable objects alight and emits a flickering light comparable to a torch, its color depending on the Magical Material. Active beam klaves have the same statistics and Magical Material benefits as daiklaves, and if a parry against a non-magical weapon achieves any successes, the parried weapon is destroyed by the heat and focused energy of the klave.

name: Reading Crystal
description: A clear, flat, rectangular crystal eight inches on a side and an eighth of an inch thick. Placed over text and infused with 5 motes of Essence, it copies the text exactly — one page every turn — and is sensitive enough to render worn, faded or partially erased text as if newly written, so long as some trace of the writing remains. Instead spending 3 motes lets the user write on the surface of the crystal, which records the writing for the next full scene. Each reading crystal holds several thousand pages; reading costs 1 mote to activate the device for a scene.

name: Bracer of Crystal Bolts
description: A large bracer of clear rock crystal set with orichalcum inlays, holding two bolts also made of enchanted rock crystal that the wearer can fire with a thought; spending 1 mote draws the bolts back to the weapon. If either bolt is damaged or broken it repairs itself within a few hours. Committing 4 motes activates the bracer, resizes it to fit and allows the wearer to fire it, after which it can only be removed by the wearer or upon her death; it has a setting for a single Hearthstone. It uses the Thrown Ability, to which Thrown Charms apply: Acc +2, 6L (armor-piercing), Rate 2, Range 100.

name: Fire Claw
description: An orichalcum bracelet set with a large red stone that fits perfectly on the wrist of a Dragon King and is not uncomfortable worn by an Exalt. Expend 2 motes to make a curving blade of golden sunfire spring forth and arc in front of the wearer's hand (a diceless reflexive action); the claw endures for one full scene and can be made to exist indefinitely for 2 motes per scene. A wearer must commit 5 motes of Essence to use it, and it contains a setting for a single Hearthstone. It is wielded with the Melee Ability and cannot be used as a claw-type weapon for the purposes of Tiger Style or Lunar natural fighting techniques. Stats: Spd +2 (+3 for a Dragon King or Solar), Acc +2 (+3), +5L, Def +1 (+2), Min S••, D•••.

name: Swordstick
description: A long, flat club of semi-living wood with a row of iron-hard thorns along either side, just like the teeth in the jaws of a sawfish; the Dragon Kings' vegetative technology grows low bushes that produce a cluster of three or four swordsticks every two years. Empowered with 4 motes of committed Essence it comes to life: the thorns ooze a sap that makes all wounds exceptionally painful (+1 wound penalties for the rest of the scene, once per scene) and the club-like blade bends itself to the user's will, aiding his attacks. Stats: Spd +2, Acc +1, +5L, Def +1, Min S•••.

name: Crystal Warclub
description: A flattened angular club of smoky quartz set with a single row of bright ruby crystals on both of its two blade-like edges. When activated by spending 2 motes of Essence, a triangular blade of glowing energy issues from each crystal and remains for the next full scene. Anyone who wields the club must also commit 6 motes of Essence to it. Stats: Spd +3 (+4 for a Dragon King or Solar), Acc +2 (+3), +9L (+10L), Def +0, Min S•••, D•••.

name: Necklace of Solar Charisma
description: A necklace of golden circular crystals connected by slender orichalcum chains. When the wearer attunes it by committing 3 motes of Essence, he becomes infused with a small fraction of the Unconquered Sun's majesty: three dice on all Charisma and Appearance rolls, and everyone with a permanent Essence less than the wearer's regards him as attractive and not in any way odd or disturbing (a Dragon King would be a cause for wonder, not of fear or disgust). It has a setting for a single Hearthstone; its crystals are inscribed with images of the Unconquered Sun, and loyal followers of the Immaculate Dragons would never consider wearing it.

name: Essence Storing Crystal
description: A flat collar of triangular crystals that sits on the Dragon Kings' shoulders, at the base of the neck, storing and concentrating Essence to give the wearer access to an extra 8 motes of Essence used just like ordinary Essence. It is particularly attuned to Dragon Kings and cannot be used by Exalts or other Essence users. It costs nothing to attune; when the wearer first puts it on and places at least 1 mote in it, it automatically sizes itself and closes when the ends are touched together, and the crystals glow softly when filled with Essence.

name: Globe of Transport
description: A solid sphere of violet crystal the size of a large orange with a setting for a single Hearthstone, carried around as easily as any small item. With a Hearthstone of at least level 2 in the setting and 7 motes of Essence, it expands into a thin-walled hollow globe nearly three yards in diameter around the user and up to two other people she is touching (maximum 800 pounds), traveling at up to 100 miles per hour to any place the controller has visited or in a chosen direction, powered for one journey. The walls are fairly fragile, providing only 3L/3B armor for the occupants, but any cracks or damage repair themselves in seconds; no one inside can attack out of it, and it lands and deactivates at its destination, depositing everyone unharmed.

name: Obsidian Sheath
description: A lightweight suit of articulated plate made from a glassy yet flexible black stone, similar in appearance to obsidian and trimmed with orichalcum; it provides the orichalcum Magical Material bonus when attuned by a Solar or a Dragon King. When worn by a living creature who expends 6 motes of Essence to attune to it, the armor bonds with its user, acting like a second skin. It has soak 8/8, mobility penalty -0 and fatigue 1, and raises the wearer's Strength to 8 (or by +2 if it is already 8 or greater). Very tough and maneuverable, it is associated with service to the Unconquered Sun and has a hardness of 4 (half its lethal soak).

name: Crushfist
description: An artifact hand-to-hand weapon and clinch enhancer that does piercing damage. Stats: Speed -5, Acc +0, +4L, Def +3, Rate 1, Min Str ••.

name: Short Daiklave
description: An artifact hand-to-hand weapon. Stats: Speed +3, Acc +4, +4L, Def +1, Rate 6, Min Str •.

name: God-Kicking Boot
description: An artifact hand-to-hand weapon. Stats: Speed -2, Acc +2, +6L, Def +1, Rate 3, Min Str ••.

name: Grand Goremaul
description: An artifact hand-to-hand weapon that does piercing damage. Stats: Speed +10, Acc +0, +9L, Def +1, Rate 3, Min Str ••••.

name: Infinite Jade Chakram
description: An artifact thrown weapon that returns instantly after being thrown. Stats: Acc +1, +4L, Rate 4, Range 50, Min Str •.

name: Charm against Disease
description: A talisman carried on the character's person that adds one die to the Stamina + Resistance roll to withstand disease and one die to the Stamina + Endurance roll to overcome its effects. Used to protect a household, it adds two dice to the Stamina + Resistance rolls of all those within, but only so long as they remain inside the warded house. Very strong charms against disease have double or even triple these effects.

name: Dragon Tear Tiara
description: Tiaras and circlets forged from all the Magical Materials, each with a setting for a Hearthstone located directly over the character's Caste Mark. They require the commitment of 2 motes of Essence to activate the Hearthstone and the tiara's own powers. When activated, a tiara adds 1 die to the character's Perception for normal perception rolls, a bonus that increases to 3 dice when she performs geomancy, astrology, detects spirits or otherwise attempts tasks requiring occult sensitivity.

name: Good Luck Charm
description: A talisman that doesn't so much give a character good luck as protect him from bad luck: once per story, a good luck charm protects the character from the negative effects of a botch, either one the player rolls or one another player rolls that would hurt the character carrying the talisman. Very powerful good luck charms will negate two or more botches in a single story.

name: Hearthstone Amulet
description: Amulets forged from the Five Magical Materials but too small to provide special benefits based on their material, each with a setting for a single Hearthstone. A character wearing such an amulet against her skin gains the basic benefits of a Hearthstone — the ability to regain Essence more quickly. Committing 1 mote of Essence makes the amulet resonate and activates the Hearthstone; if the amulet is removed, the benefit dissipates.

name: Walkaway
description: Naturally occurring talismans created from mementos of a memorable accident where the survivors should have been killed or maimed but instead emerged unharmed. Once per story, an effective walkaway negates one success on a single, life-threatening damage roll; very powerful walkaways can negate two or even three successes, all from the same damage roll.

name: Warding Charms
description: Talismans that protect against a particular type of being — Fair Folk, spirits and elementals, demons, or the walking dead. Each causes beings of the appropriate type to suffer a -1 penalty to all their dice pools when attempting to affect the wearer; very powerful warding charms may double or even triple this effect. Magical beings can sense when an individual is warded against their power and often react with hostility.

name: Hearthstone Bracers
description: A pair of bracers, one with a setting for a single Hearthstone and the other imbued with magical power, providing powerful defensive bonuses that only work for an Exalted of the appropriate type. They require the commitment of 4 motes of Essence (2 for each bracer) and will not activate unless worn as a pair. The bonus depends on the material: orichalcum adds 2 to all attack damage, moonsilver adds 2 to lethal soak, jade adds 2 to base initiative, starmetal adds 1 to weapon attack, defense and initiative rolls, and soulsteel decreases a target's soak by 2 against the Abyssal's attacks, never below 0.

name: Slayer Khatar
description: The ultimate destructive weapon, forged with the aid of earth elementals from steel alloyed with yellow jade and orichalcum. It requires no commitment of Essence and can be used by any being, mortal or Exalted, though its powers truly blossom in the hands of an Exalted. It has no more effect on characters, even armored ones, than a normal khatar, but when wielded against objects these weapons shatter and destroy them: all damage inflicted against inanimate objects is doubled, an effect compatible with abilities such as the Brawl Charm Sledgehammer Fist Punch.

name: Collar of Dawn's Cleansing Light
description: A piece of neck jewelry — studded bands, chokers, collars, torcs or delicate necklaces — that keeps the wearer clean inside and out, negating all penalties to Social rolls that would be applied for being dirty or unkempt. Attuning to the collar extends its powers beyond the Exalt's clothing to her physical body, and its cleansing light adds two dice to Resistance rolls against disease or poison. The collar requires the commitment of 1 mote of Essence to become active.

name: Mask
description: Seemingly plain ivory face masks that have played an important part in Exalted political and emotional intrigues since the First Age. A mask allows an Exalt to alter her appearance to look like anyone she wishes and completely control the emotions her face shows, adding four dice to her Intelligence + Larceny pool for any attempt at disguise. Once attuned, at the normal cost of 5 motes for a Level •• item, it also grants an extra four dice to any attempt to misdirect another as to the wearer's true motives, such as during certain Presence, Socialize and Bureaucracy rolls.

name: Ring of Being
description: Rings made by the great Twilight artificer Jervon during the height of the First Age, each a pure and perfect representation of the Magical Material from which it was made. No magic or power of the dead, the Fair Folk, demons, spirits or the Wyld can affect the wearer's innate form or mind — no Charm can change her, no spell addle her mind, and no demon may claim her soul while she is attuned. Attunement is costly: 15 motes must be invested, and only an Exalt can attune to a ring made of the appropriate Magical Material.

name: Wings of the Raptor
description: A set of wings that appears as a heavy cloak when not in use; expending 10 motes of Essence transforms it into a glorious set of wings 20 feet across from wingtip to wingtip, granting its wearer the power of flight. The Exalt may move at five times his base running speed (80 miles per hour flying) and adds six dice to any Dexterity roll involving aerial maneuvering, including dodging and hand-to-hand combat, plus six extra dice on all sight-based Perception rolls; all modifiers due to distance are reduced by three. The spent Essence cannot be reclaimed until the wings return to their mundane state.

name: Soul Mirror
description: A soulsteel grand daiklave forged by the Lover Clad in Raiment of Tears, sharing a grand daiklave's statistics and attunement cost, with an additional Hearthstone setting on the handle (four total). On striking an opponent it drains one point of temporary Willpower and a number of motes of Essence equal to its wielder's permanent Essence, half (rounded down) passed to the bearer. When it takes a life the victim's ghost is drawn into the blade rather than passing to the Underworld, and the wielder may consume a contained soul to add 1 to the weapon's speed, accuracy and damage for seven days, up to four souls at a time. Those who face it in battle must succeed at a Willpower roll — difficulty 4 for mortals, 3 for Exalted and other magical beings, 2 for Solars or Abyssals — or suffer a four-die penalty to attack rolls.

name: Soulsteel Net
description: A net of soulsteel mesh — threads woven from the corpus of other ghosts — attached in the center to a cord of woven soulsteel threads and fired by the Deathlords from large bone tubes. Capturing targets requires a Dexterity + Archery roll at difficulty 3 and catches all those in a five-foot radius (enough space to capture up to five people standing close together); characters caught lose 1 mote of Essence per turn. Escaping involves doing five health levels of damage to the net, which is difficult as it has a lethal soak of 15 and a bashing soak of 30, and a soulsteel net can hold a creature with a Strength of up to 20.
source: Book of Bone and Ebony p.114

name: Soulsteel Mesh Swathing
description: Chain swathing made of soulsteel mesh, all but unbreakable and so heavy that only Essence channelers who attune themselves to the armor can wear it (and avoid its Essence-draining effects). In addition to the standard benefits of wearing soulsteel, soulsteel swathing imparts a hardness of 4 and a soak of 13L/16B, and requires Resources (or Artifact) ••••• to purchase.
source: Book of Bone and Ebony p.114

name: Windhands Gemstone
rating_notes: Manse ••• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: Perfectly clear, so clear that it becomes invisible if submerged in clear water. The bearer's reflexes are enhanced, letting him knock aside or dodge arrows and thrown attacks with casual ease: whenever he is subject to a ranged attack he may make a reflexive roll to dodge or parry it (his option) at his full Dexterity + (Dodge or his highest combat Ability, whichever he chooses).

name: Gem of Sapphire and Emerald
rating_notes: Manse ••••• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: A gem with no constant colour — depending on the angle it appears pale or brilliant, cloudy or translucent, green or blue. The bearer is treated as if constantly under the effects of the spell Sapphire Countermagic: Terrestrial Circle spells cast at her are snuffed out instantly and Celestial Circle spells that target her are torn asunder. It protects the bearer only — she cannot disrupt spells that do not include her in their effects, nor tear apart already-extant magic.

name: Salt-Gem of the Spirit's Eye
rating_notes: Manse •• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: White and porous, like salt or chalk, but like all Hearthstones almost impossible to mar without enchanted tools. The bearer is very difficult for unmanifested spirits to perceive: a spirit not actively looking for him will overlook him, and one that is looking suffers +1 difficulty on Perception + Awareness rolls to spot him (if he is using Stealth). An unmanifested spirit attacking him does so at a -2 dice penalty. No effect on spirits that have donned physical form.

name: Gem of Adamant Skin
rating_notes: Manse •••• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: A glittering, flawless black ovoid. The bearer cannot be cut or have her bones broken: lethal damage done to her is automatically converted to bashing before soak is applied. No effect on aggravated damage.

name: Gem of the Calm Heart
rating_notes: Manse • (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: Teardrop shaped and the bright, glittering red of heart's blood. It banks the fires of the bearer's heart, letting him act out of reason rather than anger: he may spend Willpower to suppress a Valor check without adding to his Limit. No effect on Limit Break conditions.

name: Jewel of Hungry Fire
rating_notes: Manse •• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: Bright orange-red around the edges, deepening to a glowing brick red at the centre like the coals of a banked fire. The Hearthstone draws heat and flame into itself: add 6 to the bearer's soak when applying damage from fire attacks.

name: The Freedom Stone
rating_notes: Manse ••• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: Murky blue-black and full of shifting colours, like lake water rich with algae. The bearer can never be physically restrained: shackles fall from her wrists, the knots of lassos and nooses come undone when drawn tight, and all grapple, clinch, hold and throw manoeuvres against her automatically fail. She cannot be RESTRAINED — she can still be confined, as the stone does nothing against locked doors and barred gates.

name: Seacalm Gemstone
rating_notes: Manse •••• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: A fist-sized drop of brilliant azure seawater caught in perfect stasis. The bearer has incredible luck at sea: no matter how severe the weather or how poor the handling, her ship will never founder and emerges totally unscathed. This protects only against weather — not shoals, pirates or anything of the sort. More powerful than it sounds: she can ride before a gale under full sail with no fear of ripped cloth or snapped masts.

name: Stone of Healing
rating_notes: Manse • (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: A healthy earth-brown mottled with spots of green, round enough to have come from the bottom of any streambed were the colours not so vibrant. It enhances the medical talents and knowledge of whoever bears it, making an unskilled character a skilled surgeon and a gifted doctor a brilliant healer: add three dice to all the bearer's Medicine rolls.

name: Gem of Incomparable Wellness
rating_notes: Manse ••••• (bought with the Manse Background, not Artifact)
description: A brilliant emerald stone of unearthly appearance, constantly changing shape as it grows outward from its ever-shrinking centre. The bearer cannot die: he regenerates one health level per turn even if rendered into ash (aggravated damage takes up to a minute per level), never sickens and never ages, and cannot drown, suffocate, starve or dehydrate. He can be destroyed only if the Hearthstone is broken, if the Manse is damaged enough that the stone goes inactive, or if the item the stone is set in is separated from him long enough for the committed Essence to dissipate (about a day).

name: Daiklave
description: The traditional weapon of the Exalted: an elaborately decorated double-edged blade over four feet long and six or more inches wide, forged from steel alloyed with one of the Five Magical Materials and far too large for a mortal to wield. In an Exalt's hands the material resonates with her anima, making the blade light and wieldy. Each is unique, named, and treated as an honoured companion. Most have a setting for a single Hearthstone. Commit 5 motes to attune, which takes at least 20 minutes of handling and lapses if the wielder does not make daily skin contact; unattuned it is a 20-pound burden. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Grand Daiklave
description: The battleblade or foecutter — a two-handed weapon with a blade six feet long and over a foot wide, wieldable at all only through the lightening effects of Essence, and even then only by the physically strongest of the Exalted. Never popular even in the First Age, but there have always been those willing to sacrifice defence and speed for the ultimate in killing power. Most bear settings for three Hearthstones and require the commitment of 8 motes rather than the usual 5. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Reaver Daiklave
description: A cleaver-like single-edged blade four feet long and in some cases a foot wide, with a square or angled tip — slow and clumsy compared to a normal daiklave, but brutally powerful and capable of shearing through even the heaviest armour. Like normal daiklaves it typically has a setting for a single Hearthstone and requires 5 committed motes. Most popular in the First Age among the Dragon-Blooded and the Lunar Exalted, and favoured among them still. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Dire Lance
description: The daiklave-grade spear. Like every weapon of this family it is much larger and swifter than its mortal equivalent, requires 5 committed motes to attune, and is almost always forged with a setting for a Hearthstone. Its statblock prints two lines — wielded as a spear, and couched as a lance. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Goremaul
description: The daiklave-grade hammer or mace, much larger and swifter than its mortal equivalent. Requires the commitment of 5 motes of Essence, and is almost always forged with a setting for a Hearthstone. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Grimcleaver
description: The daiklave-grade axe, much larger and swifter than its mortal equivalent. Requires the commitment of 5 motes of Essence, and is almost always forged with a setting for a Hearthstone. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Serpent-Sting Staff
description: The daiklave-grade seven-section staff, much larger and swifter than its mortal equivalent. Requires the commitment of 5 motes of Essence, and is almost always forged with a setting for a Hearthstone. Its minimums are Dexterity and Martial Arts rather than Strength. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Smashfist
description: The daiklave-grade cestus, much larger and swifter than its mortal equivalent. Requires the commitment of 5 motes of Essence, and is almost always forged with a setting for a Hearthstone. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Short Powerbow
description: A baroque bow laminated from horn, rare woods and the Five Magical Materials — what a daiklave is to a sword. It must be invested with Essence to function at all (4 committed motes for a short powerbow), and has a setting for a single Hearthstone. Unlike a normal bow it has no maximum Strength: it yields to the weak and stiffens for the mighty, and ADDS to the user's Strength for damage. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Long Powerbow
description: The greater of the two powerbows, laminated from horn, rare woods and the Five Magical Materials, with a setting for a single Hearthstone. It requires the commitment of 7 motes of Essence to bend at all. Like all powerbows it has no maximum Strength and ADDS to the user's Strength for damage. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Lightning Torment Hatchets
description: Teak-handled throwing axes forged from moonsilver and white jade — the assassin's friend, and no more than an oversized throwing axe outside an Exalt's hands. They come in PAIRS and both must be activated for either to work (3 motes each, 6 total). They return to the wielder's hands after being thrown, whirling back at the end of the turn unless blocked or more than 100 yards away, in which case they can be recalled through Elsewhere as a reflexive action for one mote — and can be recalled until the invested Essence fades about a day after last being touched, which makes them easy to smuggle. A target struck is wrapped in crackling blue sparks until the end of the scene, subtracting 1 from all her dice pools; hits stack to a maximum of -3, but EACH hatchet inflicts the penalty separately. Also a weapon — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Breastplate (Artifact)
description: Mundane breastplate reforged from steel alloyed with one of the Five Magical Materials: more protective than its mundane counterpart, and lighter and more flexible through the commitment of Essence (2 motes). Soak 6L/4B, mobility -0, fatigue 0. Unmistakably magical — it glitters with the colour of the material used to forge it. Also armour — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Reinforced Buff Jacket (Artifact)
description: A buff jacket reinforced with one of the Five Magical Materials. Soak 7L/10B, mobility -1, fatigue 0, commitment 3 motes. Also armour — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Reinforced Breastplate (Artifact)
description: A reinforced breastplate forged from steel alloyed with one of the Five Magical Materials. Soak 10L/9B, mobility -1, fatigue 1, commitment 4 motes. Also armour — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Articulated Plate (Artifact)
description: Articulated plate forged from steel alloyed with one of the Five Magical Materials, with fins or long flat spikes protruding from the back and shoulders to prevent uncomfortable Essence buildup between the plates and the wearer's skin. Soak 12/14, mobility -2, fatigue 1, commitment 6 motes. Also armour — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Superheavy Plate (Artifact)
description: The heaviest of the magical armours, forged from steel alloyed with one of the Five Magical Materials and finned to vent Essence buildup. Soak 15/15, mobility -2, fatigue 2, commitment 8 motes. Also armour — see the equipment catalogue.

name: Anastacia's Chains and Catches
description: Ornamental bracelets by the Sidereal spirit-binder Anastacia, each catch a tiny lock holding a spirit or demon of at least Essence 5 — some hostile, some benevolent, with no way to tell which. A catch opens only to its own (usually lost) key or to Adamant Countermagic directed at its enchantments; opened by the key, the being within is bound to serve the opener for a year and a day. The wards decay measurably with time.

name: The Crucible of Tarim
description: A great copper vessel that distils a cast spell into drinkable liquid — roughly an hour per mote spent casting, over coal or charcoal, with plain wood doubling the time — decanted into a stoppered flask. Unstoppering it is a normal action on the character's initiative and the spell takes effect as directed by whoever pulls the stopper, making it formidable in magical duels; the Essence stays committed until the distillate is released. Learning to operate it requires the lost instructions or an extended Intelligence + Occult roll at difficulty 5 for 10 successes, one month per roll. It cannot hold Solar Circle spells and ruptures if one is attempted, dealing lethal damage equal to the motes spent to the operator and everyone nearby. It distils only one spell at a time.

name: Spirit Ring
description: A sorcerer imprisoned in a ring: a disembodied voice that only a wearer who knows at least Terrestrial Circle sorcery can perceive. It possesses only Intelligence, Perception, Wits, Manipulation and Charisma, rated by the Storyteller for the trapped individual, and knows everything the original did — enough to advise, tutor or perform theoretical work through a willing pair of hands. It sees and hears its surroundings as a normal human, trades wisdom for favours whose nature varies wildly with the soul inside, and is as hard to break as a Hearthstone. Occupants can sleep to stave off madness but are forced awake whenever the ring is worn.

name: Wedding Bands
description: Paired rings made for a Solar and Lunar marriage — orichalcum for the Lunar, moonsilver for the Solar — each partner committing one mote at the ceremony that cannot be regained until the spouse's death. Both wearers feel the other's emotional state and gain four additional dice on Social or Perception rolls dealing with the partner. The orichalcum ring adds two dice to track the spouse through any terrain without penalty; the moonsilver ring grants two additional bashing and lethal soak.

name: Horn of the Ways
description: A horn taken from a beast of the Wyld and inlaid with moonsilver; blowing it makes a mournful howl and opens a path that did not exist before and vanishes shortly after the Exalt follows it. Use commits 5 motes until the destination is reached. In the wilderness it adds +4 dice to Survival rolls to travel between locations or escape an area and eliminates all penalties for adverse conditions; used against an impassable barrier such as a fortress wall it adds +4 dice to Larceny rolls to open doors or passages and eliminates penalties for lacking tools.

name: Thunderbolt Shield
description: An enchanted target shield that adds 2 to the difficulty of melee or ranged attacks against its bearer and causes no mobility penalty, for 5 committed motes — doubled if its material is dissimilar to the wielder's type; otherwise it works as a normal target shield. Orichalcum and soulsteel shields raise the difficulty by 3 rather than 2; moonsilver subtracts 1 from any mobility penalty the user suffers; jade adds +2 soak; and starmetal subtracts one success from damage rolls inflicted on a Sidereal carrying it, cumulative with starmetal armour.

name: Traveler's Staff
description: A gnarled branch from an ancient tree, usable as a normal quarterstaff, though that is not its purpose. Planted into the earth at sunset for 5 committed motes it grows into a full-size fruit tree — usually apple — bearing enough ripe fruit to feed the Exalt and several companions for the evening, and its branches yield readily burning firewood. Come morning she cuts a large branch to replace the original staff; the tree dies and rots away, leaving no sign by sunset, and the Essence is released.

name: Blood Seed
description: A fist-sized hollow acorn with a razor-edged hole: the Exalt cuts a finger on it and fills it with blood, taking one health level that cannot be soaked or reduced, then commits 10 motes and sprinkles the blood over an area in a line, circle or similar shape. Over five turns, one armed and armoured elite trooper rises per turn from the marked ground; they are never treated as extras and return to the earth at the end of the scene. The seed forges no anima bond, so a mismatched Magical Material costs nothing extra. Orichalcum seeds add a dot to each Physical Attribute; moonsilver gives bestial soldiers whose fists do one extra point of lethal damage and who can follow a scent trail; jade adds +3 soak; starmetal adds three initiative and two to all attack and defense; soulsteel animates the dead, ignoring wound penalties and adding three health levels.

name: Dark Rider
description: A miniature figurine, human or animal, that appears to be an expensive knickknack when inactive. Ten motes activates it and its shadow grows to replace the Exalt's own, riding along with her for the scene: it gives two extra dice on intimidation or Leadership rolls against mortals who witness the merger and makes her impossible to sneak up on without concealment Charms. She may send the shadow away to spy — moving at her Willpower in yards per turn, or riding along inside another's shadow — and see through its eyes at will, leaving her shadowless until it returns or the scene ends. Dark riders have no Traits but soak and health levels (five levels, 3L soak), are harmed only by fire, and are dispelled by extremely bright light, including the Zenith anima and Solar Charms that burn creatures of darkness; those so dispelled are destroyed forever.

name: The Crimson Bow
description: A six-foot composite bow of crimson-stained wood and horn strung with the tendons of a Behemoth, once the weapon of the Dawn Caste archer Ai. It is simply impossible to draw for anyone not attuned, whatever their Strength; attuning takes 30 minutes' handling and 10 committed motes, after which it adjusts itself to the wielder's Strength and adds +6 damage beyond arrow type. Accuracy +4, Damage +6, Rate 3, Range 500, minimum Strength 3. Its legendary Crimson Arrows change course in flight to strike their targets, adding +2 difficulty to any attempt to dodge them; twenty of them require the Artifact • background.

name: Blackened Bones
description: An incomplete human skeleton — ribs and limb bones only — carved with runes and inlaid with starmetal, reputed to be the mortal shell of Hesiesh or Pasiap. Attuning takes at least an hour of handling and contemplation and must be renewed by handling them once a day. To use them the Exalt clearly states the knowledge he seeks, casts the bones into the air and reads how they fall, receiving a vision of past, present or future; simple questions give straightforward answers and complex ones unfold in dreamlike symbols, always accurate but often hard to interpret. He is comatose throughout — a few minutes for a simple question, a day or more for an involved one. The bones never reveal whose they were.

name: The Crown of Thunders
description: An orichalcum crown inset with five Hearthstone settings, forged by the servants of the Unconquered Sun for the Solar Merela. The wearer automatically receives three extra dots of Strength, Dexterity and Stamina. Ten motes adds five dice to all Social tasks for the scene; ten more issues a command to everyone in earshot that must be obeyed unless the hearer's player beats a Willpower roll at a difficulty equal to the wearer's Charisma — never suicidal, but anything short of it, and deeply resented. Ten motes invokes the crown's aura: normal humans can take no action but look on in fascination, and an Exalted witness must make a Wits + Valor roll at a difficulty equal to the wearer's Charisma or be struck with terror at the thought of harming her, resistible for one temporary Willpower, though all actions against her remain at +1 difficulty.

name: Mantle of Brigid
rating_notes: N/A — a plot device; owned through the Legendary Artifact 10-pt Merit
description: A seven-foot by six-foot section of the finest scarlet silk, faded and worn with centuries of use and embroidered with hair-fine orichalcum thread, bearing the silhouette of a woman believed to be Brigid the Magic Bearer. It may be the cloak she was given in the East or the most elaborate forgery ever made; it is possibly the single most studied artifact known to the Exalted, and the controversy over it still rages. It was the Empress's personal possession and a regular part of her wardrobe when working magic. If it truly works: it increases the Essence of any being wearing it by 5, with Personal and Peripheral pools refigured accordingly, those extra motes available only while it is worn and spent from personal stores first — and if the mantle is removed after the magician has spent more than her own stores and not yet regenerated them, she takes bashing damage equal to the difference, soaked with Stamina alone and reducible by no armour, Charm or sorcery. It also lifts the wearer one circle of sorcery: those who could work none, such as mortals, gain the Terrestrial Circle; Terrestrial-only casters such as the Dragon-Blooded gain the Celestial; Lunars and Sidereals gain all three. Solars and Abyssals, who already reach all three, gain nothing. The mantle grants only the ABILITY to use these spells and Charms — they must still be learned as usual.

name: The Sword of Ice
rating_notes: N/A — a plot device; owned through the Legendary Artifact 10-pt Merit
description: A legendary blade said to be tied not only to the past but also to the future. Brigid, the First Sorcerer, reputedly bore this sword — cool to the touch and constructed of purest crystal — until the day of her death. Extreme in both its beauty and its power, the weapon seemed to grow in its abilities even as Brigid expanded hers, and it served the Mother of Spells as advisor and confidant as well as a form of offense; whether the power of speech was inherent to the sword, the work of some spirit bound to the blade, or a reflection of Brigid's own power and personality is unclear, but it was her most trusted friend and ally. Upon her death the weapon is said to have melted into water on the spot and soaked into the ground around its fallen mistress's body. True believers assert that it will re-form when Brigid's true heir appears in the land to claim it, and that this heir will take up the sword of ice and, after dispatching her foes, lead Exalted and unExalted alike into a new era of magic in which feats of sorcery beyond even Brigid herself will be performed and the face of the world changed forever. Clearly no true heir has yet claimed the blade — but the believers say the signs are there, in the stars, on the sea and in the deep places of the earth: the time of the heir is coming. Game effects: if the Sword of Ice does exist, it would be an item of world-shattering power, on par with the Eye of Autocthon, and its powers are left up to the Storyteller to determine.

name: The Insidious Ebon Xoanon
rating_notes: N/A — a plot device; owned through the Legendary Artifact 10-pt Merit
description: The First and Forsaken Lion's warstrider, built to equal any in Creation but modified to channel Oblivion: not forged from metal but crudely carved from Essence-hardened ebony, its joints taken from a dead giant and animated with necromancy, part idol and part armour, shaped as some unspeakable horned horror and covered in the unholy glyphs of necromancy, with midriff, forearms and shins wrapped in blackened human skin studded with soulsteel and ridges of bone shards down the spine and arms. It is the equivalent of a royal warstrider (Savant and Sorcerer pp.149, 154) in size and strength — soak 24L/24B, Strength 18 — with necromantic advantages. It may carry necromantic weaponry powered by Oblivion's Avatar, though size constraints then forbid traditional warstrider weapons. Every Chosen of the Unconquered Sun within direct line of sight loses a mote of Essence per turn to its soulsteel Essence collectors, channelled straight to the wearer. Its Oblivion-tainted fists double all damage inflicted on Essence channelers before it is applied to health levels, and each health level so inflicted steals a further 2 motes. Every 50 hours of operation its joints must be tended by nemissaries using Instauration of the Fleshly Vessel and greased with the rendered tallow of a sentient creature, or it suffers the usual warstrider disabilities (S&S p.153). Worn by the Lion himself, and most often by his favoured Abyssal, Walking on Laughter.
source: Book of Bone and Ebony p.104
